question.text: Rewrite the statement $ eg ( ( eg P \land eg Q) \lor (P \land eg Q) )$ using De Morgan's laws.
question.explanation:
De Morgan's laws state that

\[ egin{align*} eg ( P \land Q) \equiv eg P \lor eg Q, \[3pt] eg ( P \lor Q) \equiv eg P \land eg Q. \end{align*} \]

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

\[ egin{align*} eg ( ( eg P \land eg Q) \lor (P \land eg Q) ) &\equiv eg ( eg P \land eg Q) \land eg (P \land eg Q) \[3pt] &\equiv ( eg ( eg P) \lor eg ( eg Q)) \land ( eg P \lor eg ( eg Q) ) \[3pt] &\equiv (P \lor Q) \land ( eg P \lor Q ) \[3pt] \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying a Statement Using De Morgan's Laws

question.text: Simplify the statement $\neg (A \lor (B \land C))$ using De Morgan's laws.
question.explanation:
De Morgan's laws state that

egin{align*} eg ( Q \land P) \equiv eg P \lor eg Q, \[3pt] eg ( Q \lor P) \equiv eg P \land eg Q. \end{align*}

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

egin{align*} eg (A \lor (B \land C)) &\equiv eg A \land eg (B \land C) \[3pt] &\equiv eg A \land ( eg B \lor eg C) \end{align*}

example.title: Simplifying a Statement Using De Morgan's Laws

question.text:
$\qquad$ $7 = 5$ or $-3 \geq 0.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.explanation:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

\[ \neg ( A \lor B) = \neg A \land \neg B \]

So, the negation of our statement is

\[ \begin{align*} \neg \left( 7 = 5 \text{ or } -3 \geq 0 \right) &\equiv \neg \left( (7 = 5) \lor (-3 \geq 0) \right) \\[5pt] &\equiv \neg \left( 7 = 5 \right) \land \neg \left( -3 \geq 0 \right) \\[5pt] &\equiv (7 \neq 5) \land (-3 < 0) \\[5pt] &\equiv 7 \neq 5 \textrm{ and } -3 < 0. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Negating a Sentence Containing a Disjunction

question.text:
$\qquad$ $5$ is integer or $5$ is positive.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.choice1: $5$ is not integer and $5$ is not positive
question.choice2: $5$ is not integer or $5$ is not positive
question.choice4: $5$ is not integer or $5$ is positive
question.choice5: $5$ is not integer and $5$ is positive
question.explanation:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

\[ \neg ( A \lor B) = \neg A \land \neg B \]

So, the negation of our statement is

\begin{align*} \neg (5\textrm{ is integer}\textrm{ or } 5 \textrm{ is positive}) &\equiv \neg \big( (5\textrm{ is integer}) \lor (5 \textrm{ is positive}) \big) \\[5pt] &\equiv \neg ( 5\textrm{ is integer}) \land \neg (5 \textrm{ is positive}) \\[5pt] &\equiv (5\textrm{ is not integer}) \land (5 \textrm{ is not positive}) \\[5pt] &\equiv 5\textrm{ is not integer}\textrm{ and } 5 \textrm{ is not positive}. \end{align*}

question.text:
$\qquad$ $n$ is not prime or $n\!\not{|} \,24.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.explanation:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

\[ \neg ( A \lor B) = \neg A \land \neg B. \]

So, the negation of our statement is

\begin{align*} \neg (n\textrm{ is not prime} \textrm{ or } n\!\not{|} \,24) &\equiv \neg \big( (n\textrm{ is not prime}) \lor (n\!\not{|} \,24) \big) \\[5pt] &\equiv \neg ( n\textrm{ is not prime}) \land \neg (n\!\not{|} \,24) \\[5pt] &\equiv (n\textrm{ is prime}) \land (n\,|\,24) \\[5pt] &\equiv n\textrm{ is prime} \textrm{ and } n\,|\,24. \end{align*}
